rows.meaning: Whole experiment run (Sequence/Experiment Begins..Ends).
rows.vrule: no value (value empty; may carry boundary flag)
rows.nl: An experiment lasting {duration} seconds involves {who}.
rows.example: An experiment lasting 10541.4 seconds involves participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: One experimental block, 0-4 (Sequence/Block Begins..Ends/N).
rows.nl: An experimental block lasting {duration} seconds, labeled {block_number}, involves {who}.
rows.example: An experimental block lasting 2537.0 seconds, labeled 0, involves participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A foreground mission/activity (Sequence/Mission Begins..Ends/<type>); type kept WHOLE though it contains "/".
rows.vrule: whole -> {mission_type} (NOT split); HED: sanitize {mission_type} -> Label (kept whole)
rows.nl: A mission lasting {duration} seconds, of type "{mission_type}", involves {who}.
rows.example: A mission lasting 347.9 seconds, of type "indiv-pan/watch", involves participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: Inter-block rest period (Sequence/Lull Begins/<type>), type=lull-deep.
rows.nl: A between-block rest period lasting {duration} seconds, of type "{lull_type}", involves {who}.
rows.example: A between-block rest period lasting 231.2 seconds, of type "lull-deep", involves participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A pause in the comm-chatter (textcomm) task (Comms/Lull Begins..Ends).
rows.nl: A pause in the comm-chatter communication task, lasting {duration} seconds, involves {who}.
rows.example: A pause in the comm-chatter communication task, lasting 23.7 seconds, involves participant Echo.

rows.meaning: An active period in the comm-chatter task (Comms/Action Sequence Begins..Ends).
rows.nl: An active-engagement period in the "comm-chatter" side task, lasting {duration} seconds, involves {who}.
rows.example: An active-engagement period in the "comm-chatter" side task, lasting 424.5 seconds, involves participant Echo.

rows.meaning: Red warning indicator light is ON for an interval (Indicators/On..Off).
rows.nl: A red visual warning is shown on {who}'s screen, lasting {duration} seconds.
rows.example: A red visual warning is shown on participant Delta's screen, lasting 51.5 seconds.

rows.meaning: Response window opens on the warning-light task (Indicators/DemandsResponse); fires just before the light is drawn, so the red visual presentation itself is the indicator_light interval.
rows.nl: The warning-light task opens a response window for {who}.
rows.example: The warning-light task opens a response window for participant Delta.

rows.meaning: The warning-light on-interval / response window closes (Indicators/Time Is Up); emitted unconditionally at every close, so it is NOT a miss (the miss is a separate Missed Action -> action/missed).
rows.nl: The warning-light response window for {who} closes.
rows.example: The warning-light response window for participant Delta closes.

rows.meaning: The system reassigns the attended side-task set AND presents a visual instruction to the participant ('starting now, your side tasks are the ...', 1259-1281) and fades the region indicators. value = the sanitized active-region-set token; region names contain hyphens so it is a single label, NOT separable into per-task groups.
rows.vrule: whole -> {active_tasks} (single sanitized token; NOT splittable - region names themselves contain hyphens, e.g. satellite-map-icons)
rows.nl: {who} is shown an instruction to attend to the side task set "{active_tasks}".
rows.example: participant Delta is shown an instruction to attend to the side task set "satellite-map-icons-sounds".

rows.meaning: The satellite-map side task is available (enabled), from Enabled until Disabled (per participant).
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: pair Enabled -> Disabled per participant; duration = enabled window; unmatched -> cap at block end. Drops the disabled event.
rows.nl: The satellite-map task is enabled for {who} for {duration} seconds.
rows.example: The satellite-map task is enabled for participant Delta for 210.4 seconds.

rows.meaning: An icon is present on the satellite map, Add Icon->Remove Icon (by identifier); the target/distractor role is decided randomly at removal and is not recoverable from the add marker, so no Target is asserted. color+direction parsed from the Add marker.
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: pair Add Icon -> Remove Icon by {identifier}; duration = present time; unmatched -> cap at block end. Sanitize {icon} -> Label. Drops the remove-icon event.; + color and direction parsed from the Add Icon marker -> color/direction columns
rows.nl: A "{icon}" icon is present on the satellite map shown to {who} for {duration} seconds.
rows.example: A "warning sign" icon is present on the satellite map shown to participant Delta for 13.0 seconds.

rows.meaning: A WRITTEN (visual) comm/system sentence is presented (Stimulus/Visual/Language/Sentence). modality branches the presentation tag.
rows.vrule: split on "/" -> {modality}/{kind}; modality=written->Visual; {kind} label (empty->omit paren); HED {kind_tag}: target->Target, distractor->Distractor, question->Label/question, probe->Label/probe, empty->omit tag
rows.nl: A written sentence stimulus ({kind}) is presented to {who}.
rows.example: A written sentence stimulus (distractor) is presented to participant Echo.

rows.meaning: A SPOKEN (auditory) comm sentence is presented (Stimulus/Auditory/Language/Sentence). modality->Auditory.
rows.vrule: split on "/" -> {modality}/{kind}; modality=spoken->Auditory; {kind} label; HED {kind_tag}: target->Target, distractor->Distractor, question->Label/question, probe->Label/probe, empty->omit tag
rows.nl: A spoken sentence stimulus ({kind}) is presented to {who}.
rows.example: A spoken sentence stimulus (target) is presented to participant Delta.

rows.meaning: A sound is played from a direction (Stimulus/Auditory/File/"*.wav", Direction/{Left,Right,Back}).
rows.vrule: split on "/" -> {sound_file}/{direction}; HED: sanitize {sound_file} and {direction} -> Label
rows.nl: A sound "{sound_file}" is played to {who} from the {direction} direction.
rows.example: A sound "dog_bark.wav" is played to participant Delta from the Back direction.

rows.meaning: A curbside 3D object comes into close view (Stimulus/Visual/3D Object, Sidewalk Items/Becomes Closely Visible); a candidate stimulus (not necessarily a to-be-reported target), so no Target is asserted.
rows.nl: A curbside object identified as "{object}" comes into close view for {who}.
rows.example: A curbside object identified as "tire stack" comes into close view for participant Echo.

rows.meaning: Positive reward sound, default_ding.wav (Stimulus/Auditory/Reward).
rows.nl: A reward feedback tone is played to {who}.
rows.example: A reward feedback tone is played to participant Delta.

rows.meaning: Negative penalty sound, default_buzz.wav (Stimulus/Auditory/Penalty).
rows.nl: A penalty feedback tone is played to {who}.
rows.example: A penalty feedback tone is played to participant Delta.

rows.meaning: A score counter fails/hits zero (Stimulus/Auditory/Failure); failure_file is empty in the real data so no sound plays and no visual is redrawn -> a scoring-state event, negative performance feedback.
rows.nl: Negative (failure) feedback is registered for {who}'s score counter.
rows.example: Negative (failure) feedback is registered for participant Delta's score counter.

rows.meaning: A score counter recovers above its critical mark (Stimulus/Auditory/Recovery); recovery_file is empty in the real data -> a scoring-state event, positive performance feedback.
rows.nl: Positive (recovery) feedback is registered for {who}'s score counter.
rows.example: Positive (recovery) feedback is registered for participant Delta's score counter.

rows.meaning: A PanTheCam AI agent is visible in the participant's 360 view, from Becomes Visible until Becomes Invisible (matched by identifier + participant); one interval per visibility episode.
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: pair Becomes Visible -> next Becomes Invisible for the same {identifier} and participant; duration = episode length. An agent may appear/disappear several times -> one event each.
rows.nl: A figure is visible in {who}'s 360-degree pan-the-cam view for {duration} seconds.
rows.example: A figure is visible in participant Delta's 360-degree pan-the-cam view for 4.2 seconds.

rows.meaning: Participant correctly reports a PanTheCam agent via the Gamepad A button (Action/Correct, PanTheCam/Reported Object).
rows.nl: During the pan-the-cam task, {who} correctly reports an agent with a button press.
rows.example: During the pan-the-cam task, participant Delta correctly reports an agent with a button press.

rows.meaning: A false-alarm report - Gamepad A button press with no valid target in view (Action/Incorrect, PanTheCam/False Report).
rows.nl: In the pan-the-cam task, {who} makes a false-alarm report with a button press.
rows.example: In the pan-the-cam task, participant Delta makes a false-alarm report with a button press.

rows.meaning: Reports an already-reported agent again via a REPEATED Gamepad-A button press (Action/Incorrect, PanTheCam/Doubly Reported Object); Repetitive scopes the press, not the button.
rows.nl: During the pan-the-cam task, {who} re-reports the same agent with a repeated button press.
rows.example: During the pan-the-cam task, participant Delta re-reports the same agent with a repeated button press.

rows.meaning: The system detects that a visible agent was not reported (PanTheCam/Visible Agent Report Missed); fired by the visibility loop - no participant action.
rows.nl: In the pan-the-cam task, the system registers that {who} missed reporting a visible agent.
rows.example: In the pan-the-cam task, the system registers that participant Delta missed reporting a visible agent.

rows.meaning: A trial question is active, from Create until it is resolved by a response or discarded (Queries/Create..(Response|Discard), matched by identifier).
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: duration = t_create -> first of (response|discard) for the same {identifier}; unmatched -> cap at block end. split category/correct_answer as before; drops the standalone discard; query_issue_focused and query_response remain separate events.
rows.nl: A {category} question (expected answer "{correct_answer}") is active for {who} for {duration} seconds.
rows.example: A color question (expected answer "yellow") is active for participant Delta for 8.5 seconds.

rows.meaning: A question is re-issued for immediate answer (Queries/Issue-Focused/{identifier}).
rows.nl: The task re-presents an active question, labeled {query_id}, to {who} for a response.
rows.example: The task re-presents an active question, labeled 17, to participant Delta for a response.

rows.meaning: The response phase for a question (Queries/Response/{identifier}; value carries only id, not outcome).
rows.vrule: whole -> {query_id}; outcome (correct/incorrect/missed/skipped/inappropriate) parsed from the marker action-prefix -> outcome column
rows.nl: {who} responds to the active question labeled {query_id}.
rows.example: participant Delta responds to the active question labeled 17.

rows.meaning: A trial question timed out with no response (on_timeout; marker carries Missed Action + Queries/Response/{id}). System-detected omission - routed out of query_response so the acted template never covers a non-action.
rows.nl: The active question labeled {query_id} times out with no response from {who}.
rows.example: The active question labeled 17 times out with no response from participant Delta.

rows.meaning: Recognized speech NOT accepted as a response (push-to-talk not held; Task/IgnoredResponse/Speech/<word>) - an incidental utterance, not a task response.
rows.nl: {who} makes an unaccepted spoken response "{utterance}".
rows.example: participant Echo makes an unaccepted spoken response "alpha move in front of me".

rows.meaning: A touchscreen or action button press (Response/Button Press/Touch Screen/<label> OR /Warn Agents).
rows.nl: The "{button_label}" button is pressed by {who}.
rows.example: The "left" button is pressed by participant Delta.

rows.meaning: Recognized speech ACCEPTED as an answer (Response/Speech/<word>).
rows.nl: {who} makes an accepted spoken response "{word}".
rows.example: participant Delta makes an accepted spoken response "blue".

rows.meaning: Push-to-talk button pressed to enable the microphone (Response/Button Press/Push To Talk) - an enabling act, not the task response (that is response_speech). ATTRIBUTION IS REVISION-DEPENDENT: ses-06..ses-33 markers carry Participant/ID and {who} is that participant; ses-01..ses-05 markers carry none, so participant is 'n/a' (unknown) - one person pressed the button but the marker does not say who. It is never 'both'. See issue #77.
rows.nl: {who} presses the push-to-talk button to enable speaking.
rows.example: Participants Delta and Echo press the push-to-talk button to enable speaking.

rows.meaning: Game-controller button held for an interval (Button<k> pressed..released).
rows.vrule: whole -> {button} (+ {duration} = hold time); HED: sanitize {button} -> Label
rows.nl: {who} holds game-controller button {button} for {duration} seconds.
rows.example: participant Echo holds game-controller button Button3 for 2.7 seconds.

rows.meaning: Points lost on a score counter (Stimulus/Feedback/Penalty/<n> Points); the marker is the VISUAL score-bar/riser update (score_event -> update_graphics, 781/795-799; ding/buzz here are gated off (nosound) and are the separate auditory_feedback event).
rows.vrule: split on "/" -> {points}/{counter} (points keeps sign, e.g. "-2 points"); HED: parse integer from {points} (strip ' points', keep sign) -> Parameter-value; {counter} -> Parameter-label
rows.nl: {who} loses {points} on the "{counter}" score counter.
rows.example: participant Delta loses -2 points on the "Sounds" score counter.

rows.meaning: Points gained on a score counter (Stimulus/Feedback/Reward/<n> Points); the marker is the VISUAL score-bar/riser update (same score_event path as feedback_penalty; the ding is the separate auditory_feedback event).
rows.vrule: split on "/" -> {points}/{counter}; HED: parse integer from {points} -> Parameter-value; {counter} -> Parameter-label
rows.nl: {who} gains {points} on the "{counter}" score counter.
rows.example: participant Delta gains 2 points on the "Sounds" score counter.

rows.meaning: Accuracy-based reward, NO points/counter (Stimulus/Feedback/Reward/On Accuracy). EXCEPTION to the split rule.
rows.nl: An accuracy-based reward is given to {who}.
rows.example: An accuracy-based reward is given to participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: Participant's action scored correct (Task/Correct Action).
rows.nl: {who}'s action is scored as correct.
rows.example: participant Delta's action is scored as correct.

rows.meaning: Participant's action scored incorrect (Task/Incorrect Action).
rows.nl: {who}'s action is scored as an incorrect action.
rows.example: participant Delta's action is scored as an incorrect action.

rows.meaning: The system registers a missed/omitted required action (Task/Missed Action), from a timeout or missed-detection handler - no participant action occurs.
rows.nl: The system registers a missed action for {who}.
rows.example: The system registers a missed action for participant Delta.

rows.meaning: A score counter is set to its starting value (Scoring/Initial/<n> Points, Counter/<counter>).
rows.vrule: split on "/" -> {points}/{counter}; HED: parse integer from {points} -> Parameter-value; {counter} -> Parameter-label
rows.nl: {who} receives an initial score of {points} on the "{counter}" score.
rows.example: participant Echo receives an initial score of 100 points on the "Overall" score.

rows.meaning: Auditory penalty (slap.wav percussive sound + score loss) for using the same response modality too many times (Too Many Repeats In Same Modality).
rows.nl: A penalty tone is played to {who} for over-using a single response modality.
rows.example: A penalty tone is played to participant Delta for over-using a single response modality.

rows.meaning: A driving checkpoint marker exists, from Create until Remove (matched by identifier); its move and reached events are separate events within this interval.
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: pair Create->Remove by {identifier}; duration = lifetime; unmatched -> cap at experiment/block end. move/reached remain separate events.
rows.nl: A driving checkpoint marker exists in the scene shown to {who} for {duration} seconds.
rows.example: A driving checkpoint marker exists in the scene shown to participants Delta and Echo for 512.7 seconds.

rows.meaning: A checkpoint marker is relocated to new coords (Checkpoint/Move/{identifier|x|y|z}). Uses {position} from snap_marker.
rows.vrule: branch on value; {position} = x/y/z parsed from snap_marker; HED {x}/{y}/{z}: signed decimals parsed from snap_marker
rows.nl: A driving checkpoint marker is moved, and its new position is x {x}, y {y}, z {z}, in the scene shown to {who}.
rows.example: A driving checkpoint marker is moved, and its new position is x -462.37, y 269.00, z 117.19, in the scene shown to participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A driving checkpoint is reached/arrived at by the driven vehicle(s) (Checkpoint/Reached); the marker carries no participant id and scope (single driver vs both) is mission-dependent, so {who} is a coverage default. Reach (arm-reach) replaced by Move+Target.
rows.vrule: branch on value (joint-action; split participants with "and")
rows.nl: {who} reach a driving checkpoint.
rows.example: Participants Delta and Echo reach a driving checkpoint.

rows.meaning: Report-response window opens for a curbside object (Sidewalk Items/Expecting Subject Report); nothing is presented to the subject. value empty.
rows.nl: In the curbside-reporting task, a report is now expected from {who}.
rows.example: In the curbside-reporting task, a report is now expected from participant Delta.

rows.meaning: The system registers that a curbside object was not reported in time (Action/Missed, Sidewalk Items/Failed To Report Object) - a timeout, no participant action.
rows.nl: The system registers that {who} failed to report a curbside object in time.
rows.example: The system registers that participant Delta failed to report a curbside object in time.

rows.meaning: An in-game hint/instruction text is shown to players (Task/Hint(s)/<text>) via the viewport instruction box; screen position varies (not centered) so no position is asserted.
rows.nl: An in-game hint "{hint_text}" is shown to {who}.
rows.example: An in-game hint "Agents Stay Together" is shown to participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: Stress level changes to a value (State/Stress Level/<n>.000000; value reduced to integer).
rows.nl: The stress level changes to {stress_level} for {who}.
rows.example: The stress level changes to 4 for participant Delta.

rows.meaning: Control mode reset, randomized per block (Control Scheme/Reset/<mode>); a manipulated Condition-variable (static/vehicle/panning/aerial).
rows.nl: {who}'s control mode is reset to "{control_mode}".
rows.example: participant Delta's control mode is reset to "panning".

rows.meaning: A wandering AI patrol drone is present in the scene, from Add until Remove (Agents/Wanderers/Add..Remove, matched by identifier).
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: pair Add->Remove by {identifier}; duration = t_remove - t_add; batch-removed at block end or never removed -> cap at block end. Drops the remove event.
rows.nl: A patrol drone is present in the shared scene for {duration} seconds, involving {who}.
rows.example: A patrol drone is present in the shared scene for 345.9 seconds, involving participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A hostile invader drone is present in the scene, from Add until Remove (matched by identifier); its wait/approach/retreat behaviors are separate events within this interval.
rows.vrule: PROVISIONAL: pair Add->Remove by {identifier}; duration = t_remove - t_add; unmatched/batch -> cap at block end. wait/approach/retreat remain separate point events.
rows.nl: A hostile invader drone is present in the shared scene for {duration} seconds, involving {who}.
rows.example: A hostile invader drone is present in the shared scene for 12.4 seconds, involving participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A hostile invader-drone idles/halts for a random interval (Agents/Invaders/Wait).
rows.nl: A hostile invader drone waits in the shared scene, involving {who}.
rows.example: A hostile invader drone waits in the shared scene, involving participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A hostile invader-drone moves TOWARD a hotspot location (Agents/Invaders/Approach) - the target is a hotspot, not the participant; Towards mirrors retreat's Away-from (a direction qualifier, no operand).
rows.nl: A hostile invader drone approaches in the shared scene, involving {who}.
rows.example: A hostile invader drone approaches in the shared scene, involving participants Delta and Echo.

rows.meaning: A hostile invader-drone moves away, fleeing the spotter (Agents/Invaders/Retreat); the spotter may be an autonomous agent, so the direction is left un-tied to a specific participant.
rows.nl: A hostile invader drone retreats in the shared scene, involving {who}.
rows.example: A hostile invader drone retreats in the shared scene, involving participants Delta and Echo.
